Written by a client through the JSON API.

author.description:
Who put this text here, as distinct from `provenance`, which says only
how it arrived. `provenance: agent_prompt` names a channel and was
routinely read as naming a sender; that inference is what misattributed
eleven keyboard-typed messages to the last API prompter (#31).

submit_abandoned.description:
True when a delayed prompt submission was withheld because the pane's
occupant changed before the submitting key could be written. The text is
in the composer and no turn started; the caller was already told the
prompt was received, so this is the only place that fact surfaces.

turn.description: Advisory hint only; use `pane.turns` replay as the completeness authority.

turn_epoch.description: Advisory hint only; use `pane.turns` replay as the completeness authority.

outcome.description:
`completed` means the agent became idle normally; `aborted` means it
became idle within 15 seconds of an Esc or Ctrl+C interrupt.

InputPromptKind.description: Best-effort classification of a live agent-owned input prompt.

composer.description:
Best-effort composer state. Older daemons omit this field; consumers
must treat that as `unknown`, never as an empty composer.

turn.description: Advisory hint only; use `pane.turns` replay as the completeness authority.

turn_epoch.description: Advisory hint only; use `pane.turns` replay as the completeness authority.

Reachability.description:
Reachability of a federation peer, derived from consecutive poll outcomes.

Serialized onto remote [`AgentInfo`]s so a client can tell a live peer from
one that has gone quiet. A C-like enum, so it derives `Eq`.

oneOf.description: The last poll succeeded.
One or two consecutive polls have failed; last-known agents are retained.

At least [`UNREACHABLE_MISS_THRESHOLD`] consecutive polls have failed; the
peer is treated as offline and its agents are stamped `unknown`.

machine_id.description:
Federation: the home-chosen routing alias of the peer that owns this
tab. `None` for a local tab.

machine_label.description: Federation: display label of the owning peer. Never used for routing.

machine_profile_id.description: Federation: saved-machine profile id of the owning peer, when it has one.

oneOf.description: The agent became idle without a recent interrupt.
The agent became idle within 15 seconds of an Esc or Ctrl+C interrupt.

last_known_status.description:
Federation: the workspace's last-known aggregate status, preserved when
the peer is not reachable and `agent_status` is surfaced as `unknown`.

machine_id.description:
Federation: the home-chosen routing alias of the peer that owns this
workspace. `None` for a local workspace.

machine_label.description: Federation: display label of the owning peer. Never used for routing.

machine_profile_id.description: Federation: saved-machine profile id of the owning peer, when it has one.

reachability.description:
Federation: reachability of the owning peer as of the last poll. `None`
for a local workspace.

AccountsCreateParams.description:
`accounts.create` — register a NEW credential account (in-app add-account). Creates
the config-home directory and appends an `[[accounts]]` entry to config.toml, then
reloads so it shows up in `accounts.list`. The client then drives login into it. It
stores only non-secret metadata; no credential is written here.

config_dir.description:
Config-home directory to use. Absent → the server derives a fresh default for the
kind (e.g. `~/.claude-<n>`) that does not collide with an existing account.

label.description: Human label shown in the list.

AccountsRemoveParams.description:
`accounts.remove` — unregister an account (in-app remove-account). Removes its
`[[accounts]]` entry from config.toml and reloads. Does NOT delete the config-home
directory or any credentials — the entry can be re-added later.

AgentAnswerParams.description:
`agent.answer` — pick one option of an omp agent's pending `ask` question
by driving its on-screen selector.

ask_id.description: The pending ask's tool call id, from `agent.transcript`'s `pending_ask`.

option.description: One of the question's option labels, exactly as listed in the ask.

target.description: Agent name or pane id, resolved like `agent.read`.

AgentArchiveParams.description:
`agent.archive` — take an agent out of active rotation (issue #173). The pane
is released but the session ref is preserved, so `agent.unarchive` can resume
(not recreate) it later. Rejected when the agent is mid-turn unless `force`.

by.description:
Who requested the archive; recorded verbatim. Defaults server-side to
`"api"` when absent.

force.description: Archive even when the agent is currently working / mid-turn.

parked_work.description:
Opaque open-work list, stored and returned verbatim (gitmoot supplies and
renders it; herdr does not interpret it).

reason.description: Optional free-text note recorded on the archived record.

AgentForgetParams.description:
`agent.forget` — permanently drop an archived agent's record (issue #291).
Only herdr's resume pointer is removed; the harness transcript and session
files on disk are left untouched. Live agents are refused.

target.description: The archived agent's name or terminal id.

AgentListParams.description:
Controls whether `agent.list` returns the coordinator's cached remote agents.

Ordinary callers get the aggregate view. Federation pollers request the
local-only view so peers never re-export an already aggregated directory.

account.description:
Optional credential/config-home account id to resume under. Absent keeps
the agent's remembered account (a plain restart); present swaps to the
named account for this and subsequent restarts.

Optional credential/config-home account id (from the `[[accounts]]` config
registry) to launch this agent under. Points the harness at that account's
config-home directory. Must match the agent's kind.

timeout_ms.description: Startup timeout in milliseconds. Values must be greater than 3000 and at most 300000.

account.description:
Optional target credential/config-home account. Absent selects the
target harness default; it never reuses an account from another kind.

confirm.description:
Replace the source runtime only after the staged transcript has been
reviewed through `agent.session_transfer` on the returned agent.

transfer_id.description: The id returned by the prepare call. Required when `confirm` is true.

AgentUnarchiveParams.description:
`agent.unarchive` — resume a previously archived agent (issue #173). The
stored session ref is resumed into a fresh pane, preserving the agent's
terminal identity.

fresh.description:
Start a clean agent for the preserved terminal identity instead of
resuming the archived session. The operator escape hatch when the
session is gone or unwanted.

target.description: The archived agent's name or terminal id.

ClientShellSurfaceSetParams.description: Updates whether the requesting client shell receives and controls pane presentation.

command_id.description: Opaque endpoint-issued command identifier from the client-shell projection.

selection.description: Client-owned selection coordinates, validated against the pane's content revision.

events_v2.description:
Opt into the stream contract a server advertises with the `events_v2`
capability: `control` lines (`lagged`, `heartbeat`) are interleaved with
events, and entries naming a pane that does not exist are reported in
the acknowledgement's `rejected` list instead of failing the request.
Servers without the capability ignore this field.

local_only.description:
Leave out events this server relays from its own federation peers, so a
coordinator relaying this server receives only this machine's events
and never re-exports a third machine's. Servers that relay no peers
have no such events, so older servers can ignore this field.

FsListDirParams.description:
Parameters for `fs.list_dir` — list a single directory's entries, for an app
folder picker. `path` is absolute; a leading `~` is expanded and `None`
defaults to `$HOME`. Read-only; never writes or traverses recursively.

GramDeleteParams.description:
`gram.delete` — remove a message from the store for good.

Deletion is deliberately destructive: the record (and any attached file bytes)
are gone, which is what makes gram safe for a short-lived secret like a
temporary API key — send it, use it, delete it. Authority follows the caller:
the owner's app sends no `caller_pane_id` and may delete any message; an agent
supplies its `caller_pane_id` and may delete only a message it is involved in
(one it sent, one addressed to it, or one it grabbed), else the call is
rejected. A `caller_pane_id` that names no live pane is an error, not a
fall-through to owner authority.

GramFileUpload.description:
A staged file to attach to a `gram.send`/`gram.post`. Its bytes must already be
uploaded in chunks via `gram.upload_chunk` under this `upload_id`; the handler
assembles them onto the newly minted message and clears the staging file.
`name` is the display name (sanitized to a safe basename server-side) and
`mime` is an advisory content type.

sha256.description: Expected digest of the source bytes. Required by the cross-machine relay.

GramGetFileChunkParams.description:
Bounded file read. A response contains at most 512 KiB of decoded bytes.
`offset == size` returns an empty chunk; a deleted file returns `not_found`.

GramGetFileParams.description:
`gram.get_file` — legacy one-response download on the local socket. The
bytes are inline base64 and can be as large as 100 MiB. For a remote relay,
and for bounded new clients, use `gram.get_file_chunk` instead. Owner (no
caller pane) may download any file; an agent may only download one it can see.

GramGrabParams.description:
`gram.grab` — an agent claims a shared-queue item. The claim is first-wins and
atomic at the storage layer, so no two agents can ever hold the same item —
this holds regardless of identity. The claimant label is `grabbed_by` when
provided, otherwise resolved from `caller_pane_id` to the agent's identity;
that label carries the same name-semantics as `gram.send`'s `from` (a rename
or reuse moves which items show as "mine", but never lets a second agent
claim one). Fails if the item is missing, not a shared item, or already
grabbed.

GramListParams.description:
`gram.list` — read messages. The audience is chosen by `caller_pane_id`:
omit it for the owner view (everything); supply it for that pane's agent view
(its direct items, the shared ungrabbed queue, its own grabs, and its own sent
items). A `caller_pane_id` that names no live pane is an error, not a
fall-through to the owner view. `unread_only` is an owner-view filter and is
rejected when `caller_pane_id` is present.

`limit`/`before_id` page the answer; omitting both returns the whole filtered
list, exactly as before they existed.

before_id.description:
Cursor: return only messages strictly OLDER than this id in the newest-first
order. An id absent from the filtered list is rejected rather than treated as
"start at the head" — a stale cursor that silently fell back would re-deliver
page 1 forever while the reader scrolled.

if_unchanged_digest.description:
Conditional fetch: the `digest` from a previous `gram.list` answer. When it
still matches, the reply is `gram_list_unchanged` — store id and digest only,
no messages — so a polling client pays a few hundred bytes instead of the whole
store. The app polls every 6s over one SSH channel, where a full owner view is
~900 KB for ~870 messages; re-sending that unchanged payload is what made the
inbox slow to open and starved the channel everything else shares.

The digest answers a HEAD poll and is computed over the whole filtered list,
so it stays cheap and meaningful for a paging client too. It is ignored when
`before_id` is present: an older page is requested explicitly, so there is
nothing the client could already hold.

limit.description:
Maximum messages to return, counted from the NEWEST end of the filtered
newest-first list. Absent means no limit. Clamped server-side to
`GRAM_LIST_MAX_LIMIT`; `Some(0)` is rejected rather than answered with an
empty page, because a client asking for nothing is a bug, not a request.

Paging exists for the initial open: the owner view is ~900 KB for ~870
messages over the one SSH channel everything else shares, and the reader
only ever sees the newest screenful first. Search, Read-all and the unread
badge survive a windowed client because `unread_count` is reported over the
full filtered list, not the page.

only_queue.description: Restrict to the shared, still-ungrabbed queue (either audience).

unread_only.description: Owner view only: restrict to unread agent->owner messages.

GramMarkReadParams.description:
`gram.mark_read` — the owner marks agent->owner messages read: `id`, `ids`
or both. An unknown id marks nothing and answers `not_found`. A guest marks
its own read state only, never the owner's.

GramPostParams.description:
`gram.post` — the owner posts a message to agents (from the app).

`to: Some(agent)` addresses one agent directly by its unique agent name (not
grabbable); the name must match a live agent or the call is rejected. `to:
None` posts to the shared grab-queue any agent can claim. `text` is capped
server-side (~8 KiB).

file.description:
An optional file to attach, previously uploaded in chunks via
`gram.upload_chunk` under `file.upload_id`.

oneOf.description: A HerdrUp guest's post to an agent on the relaying machine.

GramRelayParams.description:
Internal gateway envelope. The reverse SSH gateway overwrites `peer_alias`
from its pinned saved-machine route; it must never trust the wire value.

GramRelayPostParams.description:
A HerdrUp guest's post relayed by the machine that serves the guest: `to`
must name one of that machine's agents, and the message is labeled
`<guest> (via HerdrUp)`.

GramSendParams.description:
`gram.send` — an agent sends the owner a push-notified message.

The sender identity is `from` when provided; otherwise it is resolved
server-side from `caller_pane_id` (the agent's `HERDR_PANE_ID`) to the agent's
name (else the pane's public id). The agent name is the durable identity — it
survives a restart or live-handoff — but it is a name: it can be renamed,
cleared, or reused, so attribution and the "sent by me" view follow the
identity as it stands, not a fixed token. An explicit `from` overrides
attribution entirely. `text` is capped server-side (~8 KiB); send large
content as a file, not a message.

file.description:
An optional file to attach, previously uploaded in chunks via
`gram.upload_chunk` under `file.upload_id`.

GramUploadChunkParams.description:
`gram.upload_chunk` — append one chunk of a file being uploaded.

Files are sent in chunks because a single request is size-capped (the app's SSH
path near 65 KiB, the daemon at 1 MiB). `upload_id` groups the chunks of one
file; `offset` is the byte position this chunk starts at — the current staged
size — so a dropped or reordered chunk is caught, and `offset: 0` (re)starts the
upload. Attach the assembled file by passing the same `upload_id` in a
`gram.send`/`gram.post` `file`.

before_ms.description: Only entries strictly older than this timestamp.

GuestInviteCreateParams.description:
`guest.invite.create`: invite one named guest to one live local agent.
With `machine`, the coordinator routes the call to that saved SSH machine
and `target` names the agent there.

machine.description: Saved SSH machine alias to route this call to.

name.description:
Guest name, `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,31}$`. Prompts arrive labeled
`<name> (via HerdrUp): `.

share_gram.description:
Share the agent's Gram with the guest: every Gram the agent sends from
the moment the guest accepts, with its files and push notifications.
Default: false.

target.description:
Agent pane id or agent name. The agent must be named, running and have a
stable harness session.

ttl_secs.description: Invite lifetime in seconds (60 to 604800). Default: 86400.

GuestListParams.description: `guest.list`: guests, invites and relay link state.

GuestRevokeParams.description:
`guest.revoke`: exactly one of `guest_id` or `invite_id`. Revoking a guest
closes its live sessions immediately.

share_gram.description: Share the agent's Gram with this guest (see `guest.invite.create`).

NotificationsRegisterActivityParams.description:
Register / unregister an iOS Live Activity push token for BACKGROUND widget updates.
The field name matches the iOS client's `RegisterActivityParams` contract; the same
struct serves both `notifications.register_activity` and `.unregister_activity`.

relay_capability.description:
Sealed `hpr1.` capability from the HerdrUp push relay for this activity
token. Ignored by `.unregister_activity`; absent on older clients.

NotificationsRegisterDeviceParams.description:
Register (or update) a mobile device for remote push notifications.

Field names match the iOS client's `RegisterDeviceParams` contract. The
`notify_*` preferences default to `false` so a partial payload never fails
deserialization; the client sends explicit values.

muted_panes.description:
Public pane ids the owner has muted on this device. Pushes for a muted
pane are skipped for this device. The client owns the set and sends the
full list on each change; absent on older clients.

relay_capability.description:
Sealed `hpr1.` capability from the HerdrUp push relay, used when the
daemon delivers through the relay. Absent on older clients.

NotificationsUnregisterDeviceParams.description:
Stop pushing to a device registered with `notifications.register_device`.
A guest removes only its own registration.

PaneHistoryParams.description:
Params for `pane.history`: page further back from a `pane.stream` keyframe
(its `history_cursor`) or a previous page (its `cursor`).

cursor.description: Opaque token naming the row the page ends directly above.

lines.description: Rows to return, clamped to 1..=1000; 500 when omitted.

resume_argv.description:
Command that resumes this agent's session after a Herdr restart. The
first element must be a plain command name.

Command that resumes this agent's session after a Herdr restart. The
first element must be a plain command name.

PaneSetPtySizeParams.description:
Sets the real PTY window size (cols/rows) of a pane and takes or releases
geometry ownership so a remote client can drive the pane size. Distinct from
`pane.resize`, which changes the layout split ratio rather than the winsize.

lock.description:
When true, take geometry ownership: the desktop TUI stops re-asserting
layout-driven winsize for this pane. When false, release it so the TUI
reclaims the size on its next render.

ttl_ms.description:
Optional width-lease TTL in milliseconds (1 .. 86_400_000). Backstop that
drops the lease if the viewer disconnects ungracefully; defaults to a
generous server value when omitted.

viewer_id.description:
Stable identity of the viewer taking this width lease. Send the SAME
`viewer_id` on the viewer's `pane.stream` so the lease is dropped when
that stream closes. Absent for legacy callers, whose lease then relies on
the TTL backstop and explicit release only.

oneOf.description: Outer popup size in terminal cells, including the border.
Outer popup size as a percentage of the terminal area, for example 80%.

socket_path.description: Absolute remote-host agent socket. Registration lasts until this API connection closes.

oneOf.description:
Omitting `pane_id` watches every pane, including panes created after
the subscription started (servers advertising `events_v2`).

Omitting `pane_id` watches every pane, including panes created after
the subscription started (servers advertising `events_v2`).

source_workspace_id.description: Workspace whose focused pane supplies the `follow` cwd policy.

local_only.description:
Return only this daemon's own workspaces, without the coordinator's
cached federated workspaces. Federation pollers always set it so a peer
that is itself a coordinator never re-exports its peers' workspaces.

oneOf.description: Internal only: the restricted reverse SSH gateway inserts the machine alias.
Effective Gram relay consent, its source and errors, and gateway state. Local only.

Owner only: invite one guest to one live agent. Never reachable by
federation peers or guests.

subscription_control.description: Stream-level line interleaved with events on an `events_v2` subscription.

oneOf.description:
The server's event ring dropped events this stream had not read yet.
Events numbered `first_missed_seq` through `last_missed_seq` may be
missing, so resynchronize from a snapshot. `seq` equals
`last_missed_seq`; delivery continues with later events.

Written when the stream has been otherwise quiet for 15 seconds. `seq`
is the hub sequence the stream has read through.

AccountInfo.description:
A configured credential/config-home account, as returned by `accounts.list`.

Reports only non-secret metadata: the account id, harness kind, label, and
best-effort usage NUMBERS. It never carries a token, key, or any credential
value.

active.description:
Whether the account is usable right now. `false` only when local usage
data proves exhaustion (Codex over quota / rate-limit-reached); `true`
otherwise, including when exhaustion cannot be detected locally.

config_dir.description:
The account's config-home directory (e.g. `/root/.claude-2`) — where its
credentials live. A non-secret path, not a credential. The app needs it to
point a login/logout at the right account (`CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=<config_dir>`).

email.description:
The account's login email, when derivable from its config-home (Claude's
`.claude.json`, Codex's `auth.json` id-token). Identity only — never a
token or secret. None for kinds/accounts with no local email.

readiness.description:
Whether this account could host a resumed agent right now, and if not, the
first reason why. `None` means NOT ASSESSED for this kind — it does not mean
ready. Only Claude accounts have a readiness gate today.

AccountReadiness.description:
Whether an account is in a state that can host a resumed agent.

This exists because authentication is not readiness. An account can hold valid
credentials and still strand every agent moved onto it: a config-home that has
never completed Claude Code's first run opens the theme picker instead of resuming,
which is how the Aug 27 bulk-switch destroyed eleven live seats. The daemon has
always known this at swap time; reporting it in `accounts.list` is what lets a
client say so BEFORE someone moves a seat onto the account.

blocker.description:
Stable machine code of the FIRST blocker found, e.g. `account_not_authenticated`
or `account_onboarding_incomplete`. `None` when `ready`.

detail.description:
Human-readable explanation of that blocker, suitable for showing to a person.
`None` when `ready`.

ready.description: True when nothing detectable locally would stop a resumed agent from launching.

AccountUsage.description:
Best-effort usage for an account. Every field is optional so the call
degrades honestly when a harness exposes nothing (Kimi), only a plan
(Claude), or a full snapshot (Codex). Percentages only — no token is read.

`windows` is the current shape (any number of rate-limit buckets). The flat
`primary_used_percent`/`secondary_used_percent`/`resets_at` mirror the first
two windows and are kept ONLY for back-compat with app versions shipped
before `windows` existed — populate them from `windows` when building this.

resets_at.description: Back-compat: when the primary window resets (= `windows[0].resets_at`).

source.description:
Where the numbers came from: "live" (fetched from the provider) or
"local" (read from on-disk session logs / credentials). None when absent.

windows.description: Per-window usage buckets (5h / weekly / …). The forward-looking shape.

oneOf.description: The session recorded the chosen option as the ask's answer.

Enter went to the highlighted option, but no matching answer reached
the session file in time.

AgentArchivedInfo.description:
The `archived { at, by, reason }` provenance surfaced on an archived
[`AgentInfo`] in `agent.list`.

at.description: RFC3339 timestamp of when the agent was archived.

account.description:
The credential/config-home account id this agent runs under, or `None` when it
runs on the harness default. Reported because a pane silently coming back on the
WRONG account is what this fleet experienced as hours of lost history, and the
only evidence was in each child's `/proc/<pid>/environ`.

account_config_dir.description:
The config-home directory `account` resolves to in the registry (a PATH, never a
credential). `None` when no account is recorded, or when the recorded one no
longer resolves — `account_unresolved` distinguishes those.

account_unresolved.description:
The recorded account is NOT in the registry, so this agent will refuse to resume
rather than come back on the default account and append to the wrong transcript.
An error state to surface, not a transient: it persists until the account is
re-registered.

archived.description:
Present only for archived agents (issue #173). Its presence is the
load-bearing signal that this agent is archived; absent means active, so
older clients that ignore the field see a normal (active) agent list.

completion_seq.description: The current idle transition completed work, independently of who has viewed it.

last_known_status.description:
Federation: the peer's last-known agent status, preserved when the peer is
unreachable and `agent_status` is surfaced as `unknown`. `None` for a
local agent or a reachable peer.

machine_id.description:
Federation compatibility field: the home-chosen routing alias for the
remote peer. This is not the peer's persisted machine identity. `None`
for a local agent.

machine_label.description: Mutable display label for the remote machine. Never used for routing.

machine_profile_id.description:
Immutable saved-machine profile id used as the routing namespace once
this agent comes from the upstream machine catalog. `None` for local
agents and legacy explicit federation peers.

origin_machine_id.description:
Persisted install identity reported by the daemon that owns this agent.
Kept separate from the home-chosen routing namespace and mutable display
label. It is an identity pin, not an authentication secret.

parked_work.description:
Opaque open-work list carried on an archived agent, returned verbatim.
Absent (empty) for active agents.

reachability.description:
Federation: reachability of the remote peer as of the last poll. `None`
for a local agent.

session_transfer.description:
Present while an agent session is being moved between Claude Code and
Codex, and retained with the final completed/rolled-back outcome until a
later transfer replaces it.

status_since_unix_ms.description:
Wall-clock ms when the agent entered its CURRENT status (its last transition).
`None` until the first detected transition, and after a restore/respawn (time in
state restarts). The app derives a compact "5m/2h/3d" badge from `now - this` (#173).

turn.description: Advisory hint only; use `pane.turns` replay as the completeness authority.

turn_epoch.description: Advisory hint only; use `pane.turns` replay as the completeness authority.

AgentKindInfo.description:
One known agent kind and whether its interactive harness binary is installed
on the daemon's `$PATH`, as returned by `agent.kinds`.

submission_verification_supported.description:
The active manifest declares a composer observation region; runtime
visibility can still prevent confirmation of a particular submission.

target_account.description:
The selected target account id, or `None` for the target harness default.
Surfacing this lets a client safely reopen a prepared confirmation without
guessing which account must be echoed back.

windowed_records.description:
Older records dropped because the transcript exceeded the transfer window.
Unlike the other fields this is not a record CLASS — it is history left
behind, and a non-zero value means the transfer is lossy and needs a
person's approval before cutover.

AskQuestion.description: One question of an omp `ask` tool call.

oneOf.description: Typed or pasted at the keyboard by a person.
Written by a client through the JSON API.

author.description:
Who put this text here, as distinct from `provenance`, which says only
how it arrived. `provenance: agent_prompt` names a channel and was
routinely read as naming a sender; that inference is what misattributed
eleven keyboard-typed messages to the last API prompter (#31).

submit_abandoned.description:
True when a delayed prompt submission was withheld because the pane's
occupant changed before the submitting key could be written. The text is
in the composer and no turn started; the caller was already told the
prompt was received, so this is the only place that fact surfaces.

federation_configured.description: Policy presence is independent of whether the saved SSH profile is enabled.

gram_relay.description: Supervised Gram reverse gateway state for this saved machine.

DirEntryInfo.description:
One entry in a directory listing returned by `fs.list_dir`. `name` is the
entry's file name only (not a full path); `is_dir` is resolved through
symlinks, so a symlink to a directory reports `true`.

turn.description: Advisory hint only; use `pane.turns` replay as the completeness authority.

turn_epoch.description: Advisory hint only; use `pane.turns` replay as the completeness authority.

outcome.description:
`completed` means the agent became idle normally; `aborted` means it
became idle within 15 seconds of an Esc or Ctrl+C interrupt.

GramDirection.description:
Direction of a gram message on the wire. Mirrors
[`crate::persist::gram::GramDirection`]; the handler maps between them so the
storage record and the public contract can evolve independently.

GramFileInfo.description:
File attached to a gram message, as returned to clients. Metadata only — fetch
the bytes with `gram.get_file`.

GramGatewayState.description: Coordinator-side state of one saved peer's supervised Gram reverse gateway.

oneOf.description: No gateway: Gram relay consent is absent, or the peer is not a pinned saved SSH peer.
An attempt (remote socket preflight and SSH reverse bind) is in progress.
The reverse forward is established and the private local gateway is accepting.
The last attempt failed or its SSH forward exited; the next attempt is scheduled.

last_error.description: Bounded description of the most recent failure.

next_in_secs.description: Whole seconds until the next attempt.

GramMessageInfo.description: A gram message as returned to clients.

expired_file.description:
The attachment this message had before the store's attachment budget expired
it: show what was there; there are no bytes to fetch. Absent otherwise.

file.description:
Metadata for an attached file, or absent. Fetch the bytes with
`gram.get_file`.

machine_label.description:
Display label of the federated machine a relayed Gram came from, when
`from` is `<alias>/<name>` and that machine has a label: the same label
the machine's agents carry as `machine_label`. Resolved when read, so it
follows a rename and covers Grams stored before it. Absent for local
Grams, for an alias without a label, and from older daemons.

origin_id.description:
Install-stable identity of the daemon/store that wrote this message (see
[`crate::persist::gram::GramItem::origin_id`]). Stable across daemon
restarts; empty for messages written by an older build.

GramRelayCoordinatorStatus.description: Coordinator role: which saved peers may relay Gram.

peers.description: Gateway state of every effective peer.

GramRelayEnvironment.description: Whether the role's legacy environment variable is set in the daemon process.

oneOf.description: Config and the legacy environment variable differ; the role is disabled.

The last reload's `[gram_relay]` section was refused; the previous
effective setting is kept.

GramRelayPeerStatus.description: One consented saved peer and its supervised reverse gateway.

GramRelayRemoteStatus.description: Remote role: where local Gram calls are forwarded.

accepting.description: Whether the effective socket accepts a connection now; `null` when disabled.

configured_socket.description: Reverse socket derived from the configured coordinator and this install.

effective_socket.description: Socket Gram calls go to; `null` when disabled.

GramRelaySource.description: Where an effective Gram relay setting came from.

oneOf.description: Disabled: nothing configured, or a conflict.
`[gram_relay]` in config.toml (also when an equal legacy variable is set).
The deprecated legacy environment variable alone.

pane.description: Terminal id of the granted pane.

oneOf.description: The granted agent came back under a new harness session.
The guest opened a shared Gram's file.

GuestGrantInfo.description:
The one agent a guest may use: the agent with this name and kind in this
terminal. A restarted agent keeps the grant, and `agent_session` follows
its latest harness session.

agent_kind.description:
Agent kind at invite time, for example `claude`. Grants from before
this field use `agent_session.agent`.

fingerprint.description:
`SHA256:` plus the first 8 bytes of SHA-256(device key), for example
`SHA256:9f3a·e71c·04bd·c21e`.

share_gram.description:
The guest sees the agent's Gram: every Gram the agent sent from
`created_ms` on, with its files and push notifications.
The guest will see the agent's Gram (see `guest.invite.create`).

used_by.description: Guest id that accepted this invite, once used.

InputPromptKind.description: Best-effort classification of a live agent-owned input prompt.

warnings.description:
Warnings collected at link time or on registry load (e.g. unknown event names,
missing manifest file). Non-fatal — the entry is kept and surfaced by plugin.list.

NotificationsStatusState.description: Readiness of remote push on this daemon, reported by `notifications.status`.

oneOf.description: This daemon cannot deliver push (no-session mode has no device registry).
`push.mode = "off"`.

Direct mode without a complete APNs key config, or relay/auto mode with no
capability-bearing device registered yet.

composer.description:
Best-effort composer state. Older daemons omit this field; consumers
must treat that as `unknown`, never as an empty composer.

turn.description: Advisory hint only; use `pane.turns` replay as the completeness authority.

turn_epoch.description: Advisory hint only; use `pane.turns` replay as the completeness authority.

PaneLinkRegion.description: Inclusive display-cell columns on a pane's current viewport.

outcome.description:
`completed` means the agent became idle normally; `aborted` means it
became idle within 15 seconds of an Esc or Ctrl+C interrupt.

PendingAsk.description: The newest `ask` still waiting for an answer.

answerable.description:
One single-select question with at least one option, and a caller that
may answer it (guests never may).

oneOf.description: Outer popup size in terminal cells, including the border.
Outer popup size as a percentage of the terminal area, for example 80%.

PushMode.description:
Delivery path for remote push. `Auto` prefers direct APNs when the key config
is complete and otherwise uses the relay for capability-bearing devices.

Reachability.description:
Reachability of a federation peer, derived from consecutive poll outcomes.

Serialized onto remote [`AgentInfo`]s so a client can tell a live peer from
one that has gone quiet. A C-like enum, so it derives `Eq`.

oneOf.description: The last poll succeeded.
One or two consecutive polls have failed; last-known agents are retained.

At least [`UNREACHABLE_MISS_THRESHOLD`] consecutive polls have failed; the
peer is treated as offline and its agents are stamped `unknown`.

origin_boot_id.description:
Opaque identity of the daemon process that produced this response.
Changes on restart and fences replies from an earlier remote boot.

origin_machine_id.description:
Install-stable identity of the daemon that produced this response.
Older peers omit it. It is a pinning value, not an authenticator.

oneOf.description:
Rows directly above a `pane.history` cursor's row, oldest first, as
base64 ANSI rendered like a keyframe's `history_b64`. `cursor` pages
further back and is `null` once the start of retained history is reached.

rejected.description:
Entries an `events_v2` request skipped because their pane does not
exist. Omitted when every entry was subscribed.

oneOf.description: A new guest invite. The secret exists only inside the two links.
Guests, invites and relay link state. Never includes secrets or keys.

closed_streams.description: Live guest streams closed by this revoke.

oneOf.description: The guest after `guest.update`.
Effective Gram relay policy for both roles. Never includes secrets.
Remote push readiness. Counts only; never tokens, capabilities, or key material.

relay_devices.description: Registered devices that carry a relay capability.

oneOf.description:
Acknowledgement for the client-shell surface interest lease. This method is new on the
endpoint protocol, so its revision-bearing result can establish an activation floor.

store_id.description:
Install-stable identity of the store this send landed in (the responding
daemon's `machine` id). Lets a sender see WHICH store its gram was
written to, so a send that lands where the owner never reads becomes
visible instead of silent. See issue #98.

digest.description:
Fingerprint of the whole filtered list this answer was cut from — NOT of
the page. Send it back as `if_unchanged_digest` to make the next head poll
conditional. Computed over the serialized messages themselves, so it
changes exactly when the answer would differ and there is no field list to
keep in step as `GramMessageInfo` grows.

has_more.description:
Whether messages older than this page remain. Always `false` for an
unpaged answer, which by definition already reaches the oldest message.

store_id.description:
Install-stable identity of the store these messages were read from (the
responding daemon's `machine` id). Present even when `messages` is empty,
so a reader can tell which store it is looking at when it appears empty.

unread_count.description:
Unread count over the WHOLE filtered list, never just the page: the app's
badge and its Read-all affordance must stay correct while the reader holds
only the newest window.

oneOf.description:
`gram.list` with an `if_unchanged_digest` that still matches: nothing has
changed, so the messages are omitted entirely. A client holding that digest
already has the list; one that never sent the parameter never receives this.

One bounded range of an attachment. `sha256` and `size` describe the
complete committed file, so a downloader can reject truncation/corruption.

`server.staged_update` — the running daemon version/protocol/commit, plus the staged (built
but not-yet-running) build if one is available. `staged` present with a `sha` different from
`running_sha` means an update is ready to apply. `running_sha` is the running binary's short
git commit, absent on a build with no git context.

agent_answer.description: Supports `agent.answer` (pick an option of an omp agent's pending ask).

agent_session_transfer.description:
The server can transactionally transfer visible session history between
Claude Code, Codex, and OMP in the same logical pane.

agent_session_transfer_harnesses.description:
Native harnesses this daemon can use as session-transfer sources and
destinations. Empty means the older Claude/Codex-only capability shape.

agent_transcript.description: Serves `agent.transcript`: an omp agent's conversation as chat entries.

api_bridge_multi.description:
`herdr api-bridge --multi` forwards newline-delimited requests over one
long-lived bridge process instead of one process per request.

endpoint_protocol_generation.description: Stable client-owned endpoint generation supported by this server.

events_v2.description:
`events.subscribe` accepts `events_v2: true` (sequence-numbered lines,
`lagged` and `heartbeat` control lines, per-entry `pane_not_found`
rejection) and all-pane `pane.agent_status_changed` and
`pane.turn_completed` entries without a `pane_id`.

gram_upload_stream.description:
The daemon serves `gram.upload.stream`, uploading a whole file over one
connection instead of one connection per chunk. Clients feature-detect this
and otherwise fall back to per-chunk `gram.upload_chunk`.

health_check.description: Whether this server supports endpoint health probes.

pane_history.description:
`pane.stream` reset keyframes carry `history_cursor` and `pane.history`
pages older scrollback above it.

pane_input_stream.description:
The daemon serves the persistent `pane.input.stream` write channel
(issue #62). Clients feature-detect this before using it and otherwise
fall back to per-call `pane.send_text` / `pane.send_input`.

ssh_agent_registration.description: Supports connection-scoped `server.ssh_agent.register` on the local JSON API.

surface_interest.description: Whether this server supports explicit client-shell surface interest.

StagedBuildInfo.description: A staged (built, not-yet-running) daemon build, as returned to a client.

SubscriptionRejection.description: A subscription entry an `events_v2` request skipped instead of failing.

index.description: Position of the entry in the request's `subscriptions` list.

machine_id.description:
Federation: the home-chosen routing alias of the peer that owns this
tab. `None` for a local tab.

machine_label.description: Federation: display label of the owning peer. Never used for routing.

machine_profile_id.description: Federation: saved-machine profile id of the owning peer, when it has one.

TranscriptAuthor.description:
Who wrote a `user` entry: the owner at the terminal, or a guest whose prompt
arrived through HerdrUp with the `<name> (via HerdrUp): ` prefix.

TranscriptEntry.description:
One chat entry. Every entry has a stable, unique `id` and a `ts_ms`
(milliseconds since the Unix epoch); clients ignore kinds they do not know.

oneOf.description:
Assistant text parts joined with a blank line; `final` marks an answer
that ended the model's turn (stop reason `stop`/`length`).

detail.description: The command or path, at most 300 characters; owner only.

oneOf.description:
Fleet traffic delivered into the session (gitmoot inbox, async job
results, advisors); owner only.
The turn's todo list; one per turn, re-sent with the same id when it changes.
An `ask` tool call; `id` is the tool call id, `answer` the selection once made.
A compaction: the agent's earlier context was replaced by a summary.

TranscriptWorking.description: The tool step the agent is running now.

oneOf.description: The agent became idle without a recent interrupt.
The agent became idle within 15 seconds of an Esc or Ctrl+C interrupt.

UsageWindow.description: One rate-limit window for an account (e.g. a 5-hour or weekly bucket).

resets_at.description: When this window resets (opaque string; may be an epoch or timestamp).

status.description: Window status, e.g. "ok" or "exhausted", when known.

used_percent.description: Percent of this window consumed (0..100), when known.

last_known_status.description:
Federation: the workspace's last-known aggregate status, preserved when
the peer is not reachable and `agent_status` is surfaced as `unknown`.

machine_id.description:
Federation: the home-chosen routing alias of the peer that owns this
workspace. `None` for a local workspace.

machine_label.description: Federation: display label of the owning peer. Never used for routing.

machine_profile_id.description: Federation: saved-machine profile id of the owning peer, when it has one.

reachability.description:
Federation: reachability of the owning peer as of the last poll. `None`
for a local workspace.
